details: Formal reliability targets (availability, TTFT percentiles, tokens-per-second floors) adapted to AI's realities: provider outages, GPU shortages, nondeterministic quality. Mature teams define quality SLOs (eval-score floors on live traffic samples), not just uptime.

explainer.lead: SLA systems are formal reliability targets — availability, TTFT percentiles, tokens-per-second floors — adapted to AI's realities of provider outages, GPU shortages and nondeterministic quality. They matter because mature teams also define quality SLOs, such as eval-score floors on live traffic samples, not just uptime.

tiers.eli5: It's the promise that a service will keep working at a certain speed and reliability, adjusted for the fact that AI models can be slow, can go down, and don't always answer equally well.
tiers.practitioner: Teams set availability targets, TTFT percentiles and tokens-per-second floors, and increasingly add quality SLOs measured as eval-score floors on live traffic samples. A pitfall is tracking only uptime while ignoring nondeterministic quality, which uptime alone cannot capture.
tiers.paperLevel: Formal reliability targets covering availability, TTFT percentiles and tokens-per-second floors, adapted to AI conditions of provider outages, GPU shortages and nondeterministic quality; quality SLOs are eval-score floors on live traffic samples.

explainer.example: A team sets a tokens-per-second floor and a TTFT percentile target for its API, then adds a quality SLO requiring live traffic samples to keep eval scores above a set floor.
